claims.text: An admin with the ROLE_GRANULAR_SSH_USER_MANAGEMENT role must create the missing group in Granular SSH Group Management before the post-pod action can proceed.
When creating a new group, you must provide a Group Name (letters and spaces only), a non-sensitive Description, and select the correct Line of Business.
Group members must be added by selecting registered PipelineHub users or entering valid non-PIPELINEHUB GUIDs, then staging them with 'Add Selected Users' before saving.
During the Granular SSH post-pod action, you must review the selected groups and target pod, ensuring no more than three groups are selected.
Before submitting the provisioning record, review all parameters and overrides to prevent provisioning failures caused by mismatches.

Prepare or update groups before the action
------------------------------------------

If the required group does not exist or has incorrect membership, an admin with **ROLE_GRANULAR_SSH_USER_MANAGEMENT** can update it in **Granular SSH Group Management**.

1. Open **Granular SSH Group Management** from the left navigation pane.
2. If you can access multiple LOBs, select the intended LOB.
3. Create a group with **Create New Group**, or select the existing group's **Edit** icon.
4. For a new group, provide:

| Field | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| **Group Name** | Letters and spaces only. |
| **Description** | A brief, non-sensitive statement of the group's purpose. |
| **Line of Business** | The LOB in which the group must be available. |
5. Add members either by selecting registered PipelineHub users or by entering valid non-PIPELINEHUB GUIDs as comma-separated values.
6. Select **Add Selected Users** to stage the users for review.

This does not create or update the group by itself.
7. Verify the membership, then select **Save Changes** to create or update the group.
8. Return to the Granular SSH post-pod action and select the updated group.

Redcontent moved to DocumentationPortal <https://docs.example.com/reference/resource-673>

Purpose
-------

Use the \***Granular SSH**\* post-pod action to grant SSH access to the users contained in approved Granular SSH groups. Instead of selecting individual users during the action, you select one or more pre-defined groups associated with the target pod's Line of Business (LOB).

Prerequisites
-------------

* Granular SSH groups are LOB-specific. The action lists only groups associated with the target pod's LOB.
* You can select a maximum of \***three groups**\* in one Granular SSH post-pod action.
* **ROLE_GRANULAR_SSH_USER_MANAGEMENT** role is required to create and manage these groups. Ensure the needed groups already exist before submitting the pod action.

Submit a Granular SSH post-pod action
-------------------------------------

1. Open the PipelineHub post-pod action flow for the target pod.
2. Select **Granular SSH** as the post-pod action.
3. Review the groups presented by PIPELINEHUB.

PipelineHub shows groups associated with the target pod's LOB. If a required group is absent, do not substitute an unrelated group; verify the target LOB and group configuration first.
4. Select the group or groups that contain the intended SSH users.

retrieved_sources.title: CloudPlatform EnvironmentService Preflight Submission and Monitoring
retrieved_sources.text:
We have now enabled granular ssh support for the LOBS/SUB-LOBS 

If pipelinehub admin update metadata for user's LOB/Sub-LOB with a 'SubHostClass' , then that users pod will have granular ssh profile by default and on pipelinehub UI it can seen as a new stage post monitoring ,

We can also setUp granualSSH as post pod action and the pod is associated with the granular ssh profile associated with the LOB/SUB-LOB under which the pod is created. For more details, please refer to [Granular SSH access to EnvironmentService PODs](https://docs.example.com/reference/resource-417)

There are use cases when the pods get moved from one LOB to other LOB or SUB LOB or use cases where the granular ssh access need to be revoked and the pod to be made available for a generic SSH , in all those cases PipelineHub supports this new post pod action that will allow the pod owners to associate/ disassociate a given granular ssh profile on the pod.

### Granular SSH User Management Dashboard:

Admins can now create/manage user lists to perform Granular SSH Access on a POD. This requires a Role - ROLE_LOB_OPS_ADMIN.

Granular SSH Group Management option is available on the left hand side navigation option. 

If the user is a super admin or has access to multiple LOBs, selecting the desired LOB will bring up the existing user lists that are created.
